summary: Tovin reports ferry from the Reach docked an hour ago; whether Maren's sister took it is unknown
A courier's body was found in the north quarter; a sealed writ from the Merchant Council is missing
The courier was seen entering Salt Market before dawn asking for a woman named Maren
Maren denies meeting the courier
Tovin gives a false alibi claiming he was with Maren since dawn buying eels
Sable states harboring a courier's secret is theft and lying is obstruction, fine of ten silver marks or three days in barracks
Sable demands the writ or Maren come with her
Maren has the key to her sister's old room in her pocket; it has been there since morning
The oilcloth message scrap was burned to ash at home
Sable orders Tovin silent or he will be silent in a cell; Tovin complies
Sable states Vosk declines the writ on grounds of ignorance; says it will not protect her
Sable refuses to read sealed writ contents aloud, citing Council seal and 'market ears'
Maren refuses to carry unspecified writ; speculates it could be a bill with her sister's name misspelled
Sable cites obstruction; sets terms: ten silver marks and three days in barracks for Pell, based on his false account of Maren's morning
Tovin admits his account was an approximation, not exactly false
Maren concludes Sable's ledger is a book of names, not laws, and that her name is in it
Sable says a name is on the writ but refuses to speak it in the fish market
Maren considers using unlicensed power on Sable and the ledger, then suppresses it; nosebleed/shakes/warden exposure cited as cost
Sable sets deadline: bring writ to barracks door by second tide bell, into her hand, or both arrested publicly on market stones
Sable and young Warden leave into rain; gray cloaks close around them
Tovin confirms they do not have the writ
Maren states someone else has the writ
Sable opens ledger, reads from it, asks Maren (Vosk) arrival hour at market; Maren answers 'before the gulls'; Sable records 'second tide bell'.
Sable orders Maren to present at barracks on Warden Row at second tide bell, ask for Sable personally, and bring 'what you declined to carry'.
Sable states writ will be served by other means if they do not comply, and she will not be the one serving it.
Sable reveals Constable Pell gave an account of Maren's morning with 'holes in it'.
Sable assesses Tovin ten silver marks and three days in the barracks for a false account; collection deferred.
Tovin admits Sable questioned him earlier by the ice house with the ledger open; he told her Maren was sleeping at the Anchor, which was true but incomplete.

Maren notes her left hand has gone numb again, as since the night in the cooper's cellar; she paid for it, costing a morning and most of a day's strength; copper taste when rain comes fast. Unknown to others present.
Maren's sister wrote three words on oilcloth three weeks ago and has not been heard from since.
Sable and Constable Pell leave the market into rain; crowd closes behind them.
Maren counts to twenty; one tide bell has gone; second bell approximately two hours out; water already turning; ferry from the Reach sailed back at half ebb.
Maren tells Tovin to get up; they are not standing there.
